- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "When an issue-mode `/implement-plan-claude` project stops (`Status: BLOCKED`), the stage session that stopped stays open after a human answers on the issue and comments `/reclarify`. It then has to be archived by hand." — cause 2 from the PR description: "The Zombie-checker cleanup ran only from inside resume hygiene, so it never ran on this path." The fix must ensure the cleanup actually fires on the `/reclarify` resume path, after Step 1 reads the plan and the `Source issue:` identifier is available.
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` Step 1 (after "Read" in full) — an explicit instruction to run the Zombie-checker cleanup when in issue mode and the plan header carries a `Source issue:` line. Additionally, the cleanup-section header at line 187 should be revised to acknowledge the issue-mode timing exception.
  Evidence of absence: Step 1 (line 15) contains no reference to the Zombie-checker cleanup. The cleanup-section header at line 187 reads "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene" with no exception for issue-mode timing. The new Step 0 bullet at line 12 describes the cleanup and defers it ("once step 1 has read the plan") but provides no runtime mechanism that invokes it after Step 1. The contract test `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` checks text-string existence but does not assert placement relative to Step 1, the cleanup header text, or an operational hook at the end of Step 1. The `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` copy is byte-identical and carries the same defect.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  Requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup invocation to Step 1, and the cleanup-section header must distinguish issue-mode timing, so a future edit cannot silently regress the trigger.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py` — extend `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` (or add a sibling test) to assert that Step 1's text references the issue-mode cleanup invocation, that the cleanup-section header at line 187 carries an exception for issue-mode timing, and that a "once step 1 has read the plan" deferral has a matching operational hook in Step 1.
  Evidence of absence: `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` (lines 245-260) only checks text-string existence. It does not assert that Step 1 invokes the cleanup, does not assert the cleanup-header distinguishes issue-mode timing, and does not pin the deferred cleanup to an operational hook after Step 1. The test at line 253 checks for `blocked on issue` in the text, but the collision check at line 254 (`"blocked on issue" not in text.replace("— blocked on issue", "")`) only guards against title collision, not against the cleanup never firing.
